steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on indoor positioning in 5G-Advanced, about the challenges and solutions for getting to centimeter-level accuracy with carrier phase enhancements. Cover the motivation, how 3GPP positioning has evolved across releases, related work, and a list of our contributions.

  - use cases: logistics, autonomous harbors and vehicles, localized sensing, digital twins, augmented and virtual reality
  - deliver positioning via cellular technology rather than dedicated infrastructure
  - design driven by industrial segments, i.e., Industry 4.0

- 5G NR in Rel-16 / Rel-17
  - 5G new radio (NR) innovations: new positioning architecture, reference signals, measurement/parameter enhancements -> accuracy down to centimeter
  - 3GPP Rel-16: precise positioning + low latency for IIoT, transportation, logistics
  - commercial indoor requirements: accuracy (horizontal and vertical) less than 3m, less than 1s latency, 80% service availability
  - Rel-17: accuracy up to tens of centimeters, latency up to tens of milliseconds for InF-IIoT
- Positioning methods and Rel-17 improvements
  - methods derived from timing, angular, power-based techniques and combinations
  - Rel-17 improved signaling/procedures over Rel-16 because:
  - i) wider bandwidth -> better timing measurement resolution
  - ii) larger antenna array apertures in massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output), mid-band and mmWave -> narrower beams, better angular resolution
  - iii) joint time- and angle-based processing helps against dense multipath in InF
- Rel-18 study item
  - ongoing Rel-18 study item: accuracy up to a few centimeters within a few milliseconds of latency
  - i) bandwidth aggregation for intra-band carriers
  - ii) integrating sidelink information
  - iii) reference signals, physical layer measurements/procedures for carrier phase (CP)-based positioning

  - earlier studies: general description of 5G positioning architecture and methods in Rel-17&18
  - one study analyzed CP-based positioning: gaining traction, complements time/angle methods, removes sensitivity to sampling resolution and system parameters

  - describe 5G positioning architecture (reference signals, basic measurements/methods) to relate NR system parameters to delay/angle error variance
  - CP-based enhancements in time/angle-based schemes + problems and challenges
  - CP measurement enhancements under continuous reference signals against noisy phase measurements

  - envision further improvements/benefits of continuous CP measurements

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The ongoing work on the fifth-generation (5G) network is aiming to extend its applications beyond traditional mobile broadband, and one of the fundamental features for this is precise positioning. High-precision positioning is expected to be needed in logistics, autonomous harbors and vehicles, localized sensing, digital twins, augmented and virtual reality, and more. It is desirable to provide positioning services with cellular technology instead of needing a dedicated infrastructure. The design of the 5G network is evolving mostly in response to the needs of industrial segments, i.e., Industry 4.0. For example, centimeter accuracy positioning will be required in fully automated factories to get precise knowledge of where resources are placed, to track moving assets and machinery, and up to product storage. So smart factories are still the primary sector for precise positioning, and an indoor factory (InF) environment is what defines the current requirements and challenges.

The 5G new radio (NR) brings a lot of innovations for this, from a new positioning architecture and reference signals to measurement/parameter enhancements, to reach positioning accuracy down to the centimeter. The 3GPP Rel-16 targets precise positioning and low-latency requirements for diverse application scenarios, including Industrial Internet-of-things (IIoT), transportation, and logistics. For example, for commercial use-cases the indoor positioning accuracy requirement (horizontal and vertical) is less than 3m, the latency requirement is less than 1s, and the service availability is 80%. The Rel-17 then aims to improve the positioning accuracy up to tens of centimeters and to lower the latency up to tens of milliseconds for InF-IIoT.

In general the 5G positioning methods come from timing, angular, and power-based techniques and their combinations. Rel-17 proposes improved signaling and procedures over Rel-16, considering that i) a wider bandwidth increases the resolution of timing measurements, ii) larger antenna array apertures in massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) for mid-band and mmWave allow narrower radio beams and increased angular resolution, and iii) processing time- and angular-based methods jointly helps to mitigate dense multipath in InF settings.

- Rel-18 study item
  - ongoing Rel-18 study item: accuracy up to a few centimeters within a few milliseconds of latency
  - i) bandwidth aggregation for intra-band carriers
  - ii) integrating sidelink information
  - iii) reference signals, physical layer measurements/procedures for carrier phase (CP)-based positioning
  - Fig. 1: 5G positioning methods, evolving requirements, emerging use-cases across 3GPP releases

- Earlier studies and the gap
  - earlier studies: general description of 5G positioning architecture and methods in Rel-17&18
  - one study analyzed CP-based positioning: gaining traction, complements time/angle methods, removes sensitivity to sampling resolution and system parameters
  - gap: critical issues of realizing CP-based enhancements not considered

- Contributions
  - describe 5G positioning architecture (reference signals, basic measurements/methods) to relate NR system parameters to delay/angle error variance
  - CP-based enhancements in time/angle-based schemes + problems and challenges
  - CP measurement enhancements under continuous reference signals against noisy phase measurements
  - simulation: CP measurements with/without continuous reference signals, 3D distance error, InF channel models
  - envision further improvements/benefits of continuous CP measurements

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The ongoing work on the fifth-generation (5G) network is aiming to extend its applications beyond traditional mobile broadband, and one of the fundamental features for this is precise positioning. High-precision positioning is expected to be needed in logistics, autonomous harbors and vehicles, localized sensing, digital twins, augmented and virtual reality, and more. It is desirable to provide positioning services with cellular technology instead of needing a dedicated infrastructure. The design of the 5G network is evolving mostly in response to the needs of industrial segments, i.e., Industry 4.0. For example, centimeter accuracy positioning will be required in fully automated factories to get precise knowledge of where resources are placed, to track moving assets and machinery, and up to product storage. So smart factories are still the primary sector for precise positioning, and an indoor factory (InF) environment is what defines the current requirements and challenges.

The 5G new radio (NR) brings a lot of innovations for this, from a new positioning architecture and reference signals to measurement/parameter enhancements, to reach positioning accuracy down to the centimeter. The 3GPP Rel-16 targets precise positioning and low-latency requirements for diverse application scenarios, including Industrial Internet-of-things (IIoT), transportation, and logistics. For example, for commercial use-cases the indoor positioning accuracy requirement (horizontal and vertical) is less than 3m, the latency requirement is less than 1s, and the service availability is 80%. The Rel-17 then aims to improve the positioning accuracy up to tens of centimeters and to lower the latency up to tens of milliseconds for InF-IIoT.

In general the 5G positioning methods come from timing, angular, and power-based techniques and their combinations. Rel-17 proposes improved signaling and procedures over Rel-16, considering that i) a wider bandwidth increases the resolution of timing measurements, ii) larger antenna array apertures in massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) for mid-band and mmWave allow narrower radio beams and increased angular resolution, and iii) processing time- and angular-based methods jointly helps to mitigate dense multipath in InF settings.

The ongoing Rel-18 study item is currently focused on investigating solutions to enhance the accuracy up to a few centimeters within a few milliseconds of latency. This involves i) bandwidth aggregation for intra-band carriers, ii) integrating sidelink information, and iii) identifying reference signals and physical layer measurements/procedures that enable carrier phase (CP)-based positioning. Fig. 1 shows the 5G positioning methods, and also the evolving requirements and emerging use-cases in the 3GPP releases.

The earlier studies focus on a general description of the 5G positioning architecture and the methods proposed in Rel-17&18. Another study analyzed CP-based positioning, which is finding traction as a way to complement the time/angle-based methods and to eliminate their sensitivity to sampling resolution and system parameters.

However, these works do not consider the various critical issues that come with realizing CP-based positioning enhancements. Here our main contributions are:

- • We describe the 5G positioning architecture, including the reference signals and the basic positioning measurements/methods, in order to establish the relationship between NR system parameters and the delay/angle error variance.

- • We introduce CP-based enhancements in time/angle-based positioning schemes together with the related problems and challenges.

- • We consider enhancing CP measurements with continuous reference signals as a potential solution against noisy phase measurements.

- • We give simulation results for CP measurements with and without continuous reference signals, for estimating 3D distance error in the InF channel models.

- • Finally, we envision further improvements/benefits in continuous CP measurements.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Ongoing work on the fifth-generation (5G) network aims to extend its applications beyond traditional mobile broadband, and one of the fundamental features is precise positioning. High-precision positioning is anticipated to be needed in logistics, autonomous harbors and vehicles, localized sensing, digital twins, augmented and virtual reality, and more. It is desirable to deliver positioning services using cellular technology instead of requiring a dedicated infrastructure. The 5G network design is evolving mainly in response to the needs of industrial segments, i.e., Industry 4.0. We can foresee the need for centimeter accuracy positioning in fully automated factories for acquiring precise knowledge of resources placement, tracking moving assets and machinery, up to product storage. As a result, smart factories remain the primary sector for precise positioning, and the indoor factory (InF) environment defines the current requirements and challenges [1].

In this respect, the 5G new radio (NR) provides numerous innovations, from a new positioning architecture and reference signals to measurement/parameter enhancements, for achieving positioning accuracy down to the centimeter. The 3GPP Rel-16 targets the precise positioning and low-latency requirements of diverse application scenarios, including Industrial Internet-of-things (IIoT), transportation, and logistics. For instance, for commercial use-cases the indoor positioning accuracy (horizontal and vertical) and latency requirements are less than 3m and less than 1s of latency, with 80% service availability. Meanwhile, Rel-17 aims to improve the positioning accuracy up to tens of centimeters and lower the latency up to tens of milliseconds for InF-IIoT.

The 5G positioning methods are, in general, derived from timing, angular, and power-based techniques and their combinations, where Rel-17 proposes improved signaling and procedures over Rel-16 considering that i) wider bandwidth increases timing measurement resolution, ii) larger antenna array apertures in massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) for mid-band and mmWave allow narrower radio beams and increased angular resolution, and iii) joint processing of time- and angular-based methods helps mitigate dense multipath in InF settings.

The current focus of the ongoing Rel-18 study item [2] is to investigate solutions that enhance accuracy up to a few centimeters within a few milliseconds of latency. This involves i) bandwidth aggregation for intra-band carriers, ii) integrating sidelink information, and iii) identifying reference signals and physical layer measurements/procedures to enable carrier phase (CP)-based positioning. Fig. 1 shows the 5G positioning methods, together with the evolving requirements and emerging use-cases in 3GPP releases [3].

The earlier studies (e.g., [1,3]) focus on a general description of the 5G positioning architecture and methods proposed in Rel-17&18. Meanwhile, the study [4] analyzed CP-based positioning, which is finding traction as a complement to time/angle-based methods that eliminates their sensitivity to sampling resolution and system parameters.

However, these works do not consider the various critical issues entailed in realizing CP-based positioning enhancements. In this respect, our main contributions are:

- • We describe the 5G positioning architecture, including reference signals and basic positioning measurements/methods, to establish the relationship between NR system parameters and delay/angle error variance.

- • We introduce CP-based enhancements in time/angle-based positioning schemes along with the related problems and challenges.

- • We consider CP measurement enhancements under continuous reference signals as a potential solution to counter noisy phase measurements.

- • We provide simulation results for CP measurements, with/without continuous reference signals, in estimating 3D distance error in the InF channel models.

- • Finally, further improvements/benefits in continuous CP measurements are envisioned.

References:
[1] S. Dwivedi et al. , “Positioning in 5G networks,” IEEE Commun. Mag. , vol. 59, no. 11, pp. 38–44, 2021.
[2] 3GPP WID RP-222616, “Revised SID on study on expanded and improved NR positioning,” Sept. 2022.
[3] 3GPP TR 38.857, “Study on NR positioning enhancements,” Mar. 2021.
[4] A. Fouda et al. , “Toward cm-level accuracy: Carrier phase positioning for IIoT in 5G-advanced NR networks,” in IEEE PIMRC , 2022.
